title: Core database connection pool exhaustion
symptoms: Many services time out at once on database calls
"too many connections" or pool checkout timeout errors
core-db active connections at the configured maximum
diagnostic_steps: Compare core-db active connections with the pool maximum on the database dashboard.
List the top clients by open connections to find the service holding the most.
Check whether that service deployed or scaled out in the last 30 minutes.
Look for long-running transactions that hold connections open.
remediation_steps: Cancel queries running longer than 60 seconds from the offending client.
Scale the offending service back to its previous replica count if it scaled out.
If one service is leaking connections, restart its pods one at a time.
rollback_steps: If a deploy introduced the leak, roll that service back with `fernctl rollback <service> --to previous`.

escalation.when: Connections stay at the maximum for 10 minutes after remediation, or write errors appear.

title: Core database replication lag
symptoms: Reads return stale data shortly after a write
Bookings or payments missing for a few seconds, then appearing
core-db replica lag above 5 seconds
diagnostic_steps: Check replica lag per replica on the database dashboard.
Look for a bulk write, backfill, or migration running on the primary.
Check replica disk and CPU saturation.
remediation_steps: Pause any backfill or migration job writing to the primary.
Route read traffic for checkout and scheduling to the primary until lag recovers.
Remove a replica that is not catching up from the read pool.
rollback_steps: If a schema migration caused the lag, run its down migration once lag is under 1 second.

escalation.when: Lag exceeds 60 seconds or keeps growing after write jobs are paused.

title: Auth TLS certificate expiry
symptoms: Sudden spike in 401 Unauthorized responses from auth
Internal callers report TLS handshake or certificate verification failures
Errors start at a round time with no auth deploy
diagnostic_steps: Confirm there was no auth deploy in the window. A spike without a deploy points away from a code change.
Check the expiry date of the auth mutual TLS certificate with `fernctl certs show auth`.
Check auth logs for `certificate has expired` or `bad certificate` errors from internal callers.
Confirm the 401 spike started at the certificate's expiry time.
remediation_steps: Issue a new certificate with `fernctl certs renew auth`.
Roll auth pods so they load the new certificate.
Watch the 401 rate return to baseline within 5 minutes.
Open a follow-up to fix the automatic renewal job.

escalation.when: Renewal fails, or 401s stay elevated 10 minutes after the new certificate is loaded.

title: Auth session signing key rotation failure
symptoms: Users are logged out and must sign in again
Token validation errors mentioning an unknown key ID
Errors begin right after a scheduled key rotation
diagnostic_steps: Check whether a signing key rotation ran in the last hour.
Confirm every auth instance publishes the same key set.
Check auth logs for `unknown kid` validation errors.
remediation_steps: Re-publish the previous key alongside the new one so old tokens validate.
Restart auth instances that serve a stale key set.
rollback_steps: Revert to the previous signing key with `fernctl keys rollback auth`.

escalation.when: Sign-in itself fails, or validation errors persist after the key set is consistent.

title: Checkout API elevated error rate
symptoms: checkout-api 5xx rate above 1%
Customers see "something went wrong" at checkout
Errors without a matching rise in latency
diagnostic_steps: Group checkout-api errors by endpoint and error type.
Check whether checkout-api deployed in the last 30 minutes.
Check the health of auth and core-db, which checkout-api calls synchronously.
remediation_steps: If one endpoint fails, disable it with its feature flag.
If a dependency is failing, follow that dependency's runbook.
rollback_steps: If a checkout-api deploy caused the errors, run `fernctl rollback checkout-api --to previous`.

escalation.when: The error rate stays above 1% for 15 minutes, or checkout fails completely.

title: Card processor outage
symptoms: payment-gateway timeouts or errors on calls to the card processor
Payment authorizations fail across all card types
No recent payment-gateway deploy
diagnostic_steps: Check the card processor status page linked from the payments dashboard.
Confirm failures are on outbound processor calls, not on core-db.
Confirm there was no payment-gateway deploy in the window.
remediation_steps: Enable payment retry queueing so bookings are held, not lost.
Post a customer status update that payments are delayed.
Open a ticket with the card processor's support line.

escalation.when: The processor outage lasts more than 15 minutes, or queued payments exceed 1,000.

title: Payment gateway latency regression after deploy
symptoms: checkout-api p95 latency well above its SLO
payment-gateway p95 latency rising shortly after a deploy
Slow or timing-out checkouts while other services are healthy
diagnostic_steps: Check payment-gateway p95 against its 400 ms SLO and compare with checkout-api.
List payment-gateway deploys in the last 60 minutes and note the version.
Confirm the latency rise started within a few minutes of that deploy.
Check core-db health to rule out the database as the shared cause.
remediation_steps: Roll back payment-gateway to the previous version (see rollback steps).
Watch checkout-api p95 return under its 600 ms SLO.
Block the bad version from redeploying until a fix is reviewed.
rollback_steps: Confirm the previous version is serving on every instance.
Post in #payments-escalation that payment-gateway was rolled back and why.

escalation.when: Page the Payments on-call before rolling back, or immediately if latency persists after rollback.

title: Notifications queue backlog
symptoms: Booking confirmations or reminders arrive late
Notifications queue depth growing for 10 minutes or more
Email or SMS provider rate-limit errors
diagnostic_steps: Check queue depth and the oldest message age.
Check worker error logs for provider rate-limit or authentication errors.
Check whether notifications deployed recently.
remediation_steps: Scale notification workers up if they are healthy but behind.
If the provider rate-limits, lower the send rate and let the queue drain.
Pause non-urgent reminder sends until the backlog clears.
rollback_steps: If a notifications deploy broke sending, run `fernctl rollback notifications --to previous`.

escalation.when: The oldest message is older than 30 minutes, or nothing is sending.

title: Calendar sync stalled
symptoms: New bookings do not appear in providers' external calendars
calendar-sync job lag growing
Double bookings reported by providers
diagnostic_steps: Check calendar-sync job lag and failed job count.
Group failures by external calendar provider to spot a provider outage.
Check scheduling-api for errors publishing booking events.
remediation_steps: Retry failed sync jobs once the cause is fixed.
If one provider is down, pause its sync and let others continue.
Turn on the double-booking guard in scheduling-api until sync catches up.
rollback_steps: If a calendar-sync deploy caused the stall, run `fernctl rollback calendar-sync --to previous`.

escalation.when: Sync lag exceeds 1 hour, or double bookings are confirmed.

title: Search index degraded or stale
symptoms: Provider search is slow, returns errors, or misses new providers
search-index p95 latency above its SLO
Index rebuild lag growing
diagnostic_steps: Check search-index p95 latency and error rate.
Check the rebuild job lag from core-db.
Confirm that only web-app search depends on search-index. Checkout and scheduling do not.
remediation_steps: Serve search from the last good index snapshot.
Restart the rebuild job if it is stuck.
Post a status update that search may be incomplete while booking and checkout work normally.
rollback_steps: If a search-index deploy caused it, run `fernctl rollback search-index --to previous`.

escalation.when: Search is fully unavailable for more than 30 minutes.

title: Web app errors after front-end release
symptoms: Spike in browser errors or blank pages after a web-app release
web-app availability below its SLO while backend APIs are healthy
Errors limited to one browser or one page
diagnostic_steps: Compare the error spike's start time with the latest web-app release.
Check backend API health to confirm the problem is in the front end.
Group browser errors by page and browser.
remediation_steps: Turn off the feature flag for the new page or component if there is one.
rollback_steps: Purge the CDN cache for the front-end bundle.

escalation.when: Customers cannot book or check out after the rollback.

title: Billing invoice generation failure
symptoms: Monthly invoices not generated or stuck in pending
Invoice job failures in billing logs
Business customers report missing invoices
diagnostic_steps: Check the invoice job run history and failure reasons.
Check core-db health, since invoice runs read heavily from it.
Check whether billing deployed since the last successful run.
remediation_steps: Re-run the invoice job for failed accounts only.
Hold invoice emails until totals are verified.
rollback_steps: If a billing deploy broke invoicing, run `fernctl rollback billing --to previous`, then re-run the job.

escalation.when: Invoices are still missing 4 hours after the scheduled run.
